In contrast, Algeria's attacking momentum increased significantly after the second hydration break, going from 0 to 2 actions per minute, which suggests that they benefited more from the breaks overall, as they were able to gain momentum and potentially put more pressure on Switzerland in the later stages of the match. This shift in momentum could have been a crucial factor in the outcome of the game, as Algeria's increased attacking pressure may have caught Switzerland off guard and affected their overall performance.
